items.title: CAC Consortium: high coronary calcium in adults aged 30-45 linked to higher death risk over 30 years (JAMA Cardiology)
items.summary: In 12,847 adults aged 30 to 45 who had clinically indicated CAC scans, a CAC score above the 90th percentile was linked to about 1.9 to 3.7 times higher all-cause, cardiovascular and coronary mortality over a median 22.6-year follow-up (JAMA Cardiology, Oct 23, 2026).
bullets: Design: retrospective CAC Consortium cohort (4 US centres) of referred adults aged 30-45 (mean age 40.5, 77% men); 72.1% had CAC 0, 12.7% were at the 75th-90th percentile and 13.3% above the 90th percentile; median follow-up 22.6 years, 624 deaths (149 CVD, 81 CHD).
Adjusted hazard ratios for CAC above the 90th percentile vs CAC 0: all-cause death 1.87 (95% CI 1.54-2.27), CVD death 2.60 (1.77-3.82), CHD death 3.71 (2.24-6.16).
Modeled 30-year risk, above 90th percentile vs CAC 0: all-cause death 12.9% vs 7.5%, CVD death 4.5% vs 1.5%, CHD death 3.0% vs 0.6%.
Limits: referred, mostly male, US cohort with no randomised treatment, and 30-year figures are partly modeled (Kaplan-Meier plus Weibull), so it shows risk, not that treating it changes outcomes.

Take-home: in adults aged 30-45, a CAC score above the 90th percentile flags premature atherosclerosis and higher long-term mortality; the authors suggest it may help guide earlier, more intensive prevention.
items.source: Choi S, ... Blaha MJ. JAMA Cardiol, Oct 23, 2026. doi:10.1001/jamacardio.2026.4819
